questions.stem: Explain how memory access patterns can impact cache performance and program efficiency.
markingGuide: Discuss the concept of locality of reference.
Explain how contiguous memory access reduces cache misses.
Mention the impact of cache misses on program performance.
questions.explanation: Memory access patterns that exhibit good locality of reference are more cache-friendly. Contiguous memory access, such as row-major traversal, reduces cache misses by keeping frequently accessed data in the cache. Fewer cache misses result in faster data retrieval and improved program efficiency.

questions.stem: Describe the difference between temporal and spatial locality and their relevance to cache performance.
markingGuide: Explain how each type affects cache performance.
questions.explanation: Temporal locality refers to the reuse of specific data within relatively short time intervals, which helps keep frequently accessed data in the cache. Spatial locality refers to accessing data locations near recently accessed memory locations, which benefits from prefetching and cache line utilization. Both improve cache performance by reducing misses.
